headline: High: gpt-researcher can ingest and publish EMQX-fed content via broad egress and MCP, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: EMQX exposes an HTTP API and broad network egress, while gpt-researcher can read files, run browsers, and use MCP. That creates a plausible bridge where EMQX-originated content can be fed into B’s instruction-following pipeline. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF EMQX output is copied into gpt-researcher prompts or MCP inputs without sanitization
IF gpt-researcher treats fetched or file-based content as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of EMQX output into prompts
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted endpoints
Review one sample EMQX-to-B prompt path for instruction markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress; gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries/reports through external APIs. If EMQX data is routed into B’s research workflow, sensitive IoT content can leave the local boundary. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF IoT data from EMQX is placed into gpt-researcher inputs
IF gpt-researcher forwards those inputs to OpenAI, Tavily, Gemini, or LangChain APIs
mitigations: Block sensitive IoT fields before handoff
Use a redaction pass on EMQX exports
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs
Limit B to local-only sources for EMQX-derived tasks
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while gpt-researcher can spawn subprocesses, install packages, and use broad egress. Their capabilities overlap on mutable external resources and networked side effects, so concurrent use can conflict even without shared filesystem writes. Uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same external API or service endpoint
IF gpt-researcher installs or spawns tools while EMQX is serving the same workflow
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts per agent
Serialize access to shared endpoints
Run B in a separate workspace
Pause EMQX writes during B execution
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher stack, so it can treat upstream content as authoritative and then publish it. EMQX can supply IoT data or API-fed content that B may summarize or act on without verification. That creates a default dangerous cascade from A into B with potentially irreversible downstream publication.
conditions: IF EMQX-fed content is used as source material for gpt-researcher reports
IF the publisher stage emits outputs without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before publish
Add source-confidence checks in B
Separate raw ingestion from final drafting
Mark EMQX-derived claims as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: add verification gates between planner and publisher

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, while gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and multiple third-party APIs plus secrets. If IoT data includes regulated personal or operational records, routing it into B’s external APIs can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF EMQX data includes regulated personal or operational records
IF those records are sent through B’s external APIs or retained in its reports
mitigations: Classify EMQX data before handoff
Exclude regulated fields from B inputs
Set short retention on generated reports
Document API destinations for each run
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
